A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that there is a high rate of CRBSI in our home parenteral nutrition (HPN) population, and that the majority are due to the use of tunnelled catheters (TCs).

we have identified that the use of chlorhexidine-impregnated catheter dressings and chlorhexidine lock solutions is effective in reducing CRBSI in patients on long-term home parenteral nutrition (HPN) and should be considered as standard practice.
